full_judgment:
On 15-12-84 the petitioner filed a complaint before the Upazila Magistrate, Tangail against the accused opposite parties alleging, inter alia, that witness No. 1 Most. Hajera Khatun, daughter of the complainant, was married to one Md. Abdul Kader of village Dighir under Police Station Ghatail in the year 1969 and through the wedlock, she gave birth to 6 children out of whom 4 are alive; that accused opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 namely, Nurul Islam and Md. Bashiruddin along with 4 others had enticed away the said Hazera Khatun, wife of the said Abdul Kader and daughter of the complainant, to give her in marriage again with accused opposite party No. 1 Nurul Islam. At this, the said Abdul Kader, husband of Hajera Khatun, brought a criminal case against the said accused opposite parties and in that case Most. Hajera Khatun was kept in the judicial custody by an order of the court but upon her subsequent prayer she was released from the judicial custody by the learned Magistrate to go anywhere according to her choice and accordingly, on her release she left for her house being escorted by the complainant and two other witnesses but when she along with her father and others had reached near the Circuit House, the accused opposite parties formed an unlawful assembly and being armed with deadly weapons suddenly attacked them and abducted the victim Hajera Khatun and kept her confined at different places to outrage her modesty. The father of the victim then lodged the complaint in the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Tangail 

 3. Then the learned Upazila Magistrate examined the complainant under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and having a prima facie case took cognizance of the offence under sections 147/366 of the Penal Code against the accused opposite parties on 15-12-84 and issued process against them and the case was registered as Complaint Case No. 423(1) 84. The accused opposite parties then appeared before the court of the learned Magistrate and obtained bail from the said court and thereafter moved a revisional application before the learned Sessions Judge, Tangail under sections 435/439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for quashment of the proceedings of the said Complaint Case No. 423(1) 84. The said application was numbered as Criminal Motion No. 296 of 1984. The learned Sessions Judge heard the said motion on both the sides and was pleased to allow the same and quashed the proceedings of the Complaint Case No. 423(1) 84 pending in the Court of the Sadar Upazila Magistrate, Tangail by his judgment and order dated 17-7-85. 

 6. It is firstly contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the learned Sessions Judge has acted illegally and without his jurisdiction in quashing the proceeding of the case pending in the Court of the learned Upazila Magistrate in exercise of his power under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, the impugned judgment and order are liable to be set aside. The next contention of the learned Advocates for the petitioner is that the allegation made in the complaint very well discloses an offence under sections 147/366 of the Penal Code against the accused opposite parties and the learned Sessions Judge most illegally embarked upon an enquiry as to the genuineness of the said allegations before the prosecution has got a chance to lead evidence to substantiate the same and quashed the proceeding of the case upon a wrong observation to the following effect. 

 "These orders of the Misc. Case in connection with the previous criminal case brought by the husband of Hajera Khatun show that Hajera was never in custody of the complainant and her being abducted by the accused petitioners on 14-12-84 from the possession of the complainant appears to be an absurd proposition." 

 Hence, the impugned judgment and order cannot be sustained in law. In support of his first contention Mr. Farid Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, has referred to a decision in the case of Mahamudul Haq vs. Golam Moula and others reported in 37 DLR 290 wherein it has been observed in para 12 by their Lordships as follows: 

 "We are, therefore, of the opinion that the learned Sessions Judge acted without jurisdiction in quashing the proceeding pending before the Sub-divisional Magistrate in exercise of his power under sections 435 and 439A CrPC. Section 438 CrPC is still in the Statute Book. If he was of the opinion that a prima facie case for quashing was made out by the accused opposite parties then he could have referred the case for an order of the High Court Division. Section 438 CrPC does not on terms require the Sessions Judge to report a matter which requires the quashing of a proceeding pending before a Subordinate Court for the order of the High Court Division. It is because the High Court Division exclusively exercises the power of quashing under section 561A CrPC that the Sessions Judge is obliged to report such matters under section 438 CrPC for an order of the High Court Division." 

 As to his second contention, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has also relied on the same decision along with a decision of our Appellate Division in the case of Bangladesh vs. Tan Kheng Hock reported in 31 DLR (AD) 69. In the latter decision, their Lordships of the Appellate Division have been pleased to observe in paragraph 22: 

 "In other words, the learned Sessions Judge embarked upon an investigation as to the truth or otherwise of the prosecution case. This is not permissible in a proceeding for quashing. The Court has to accept the prosecution case as it is and has come to a conclusion that upon the facts alleged no criminal offence has been disclosed." 

 7. We have perused the impugned judgment of the learned Sessions Judge along with the complaint and the order sheet of the case annexed to the application and heard and carefully considered the above submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and we find much force in his said submissions, particularly in view of the decisions cited above. In the instant case, we have no hesitation to say that the learned Sessions Judge has acted illegally and without jurisdiction in quashing the proceeding of the case pending in the Court of Sadar Upazila Magistrate, Tangail in exercise of his power under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure because the power of quashing a proceeding of a criminal case is only available under section 561A CrPC and not under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It further appears that the learned Sessions Judge has passed the impugned order for quashment of the proceeding of the case with some observation as quoted above regarding the truth or otherwise of the prosecution case before the prosecution has got the chance to lead any evidence. The above observation of the learned Sessions Judge is also unwarranted at the stage as he was not competent to embark upon any enquiry as to the truth or otherwise of the prosecution case in dealing with an application for quashing a proceeding. 

 9. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned judgment and order dated 17-7-85 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Tangail in Criminal Motion No. 296 of 1984 are hereby set aside. Let the trial of the case be proceeded with in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible.
